title: Iterate, measure, fix: how the system got better

iterations.title: 1. Define the answer contract first
iterations.what: The Class 6 checkpoint used our own 9-topic taxonomy. When the course published common labels, the label file, prompts, schema and golden labels were moved to v2. Code, not the prompt, enforces the contract: required keys, allowed labels, ranges, exact quotes, and every returned index.

iterations.title: 2. Human-labeled evals as repeatable checks
iterations.what: The author hand-labeled 50 golden reviews, froze them before any model saw them, then converted them to v2 by explicit rules plus 17 personal confirmations. Every model or prompt choice was compared against them; nothing was tuned on them.

iterations.title: 3. Every loop has a cost: from 1 review per call to 50
iterations.what: One review per Claude Haiku call measured $0.00085 per review (about $410 for the corpus). Switching to 50 reviews per request, a compact schema, code-filled quotes for short reviews, and GPT-6 Luna at effort none brought it to about $0.00002 per text.

iterations.title: 4. Cache what you already know
iterations.what: Exact-text reuse: 484,189 distinct texts were classified once, and 176,418 rows reuse a validated result with direct provenance. The warm pilot rerun made zero model calls.

iterations.title: 5. Measure 100 before scaling
iterations.what: A real cold and warm 100-review pilot, an offline calculator with editable dated rates, and full-run projections. The actual cost was later reconciled against the projection ($9.58 vs $7.08), with the reasons stated.

iterations.title: 6. Save states survive the unexpected
iterations.what: Each batch is saved atomically, and OpenAI batch IDs are saved before waiting. The laptop froze in the middle of the recorded run; on return, the saved state was intact and the run resumed without re-sending a single completed review.

iterations.title: 7. Run work in parallel, not one task at a time
iterations.what: A bottleneck was spotted mid-run: validation retries ran one by one (about 40 minutes per batch). They were switched to 8 parallel workers on one queue with a single writer lock (under 2 minutes), with 4 batches in flight. The enrichment finished in about 3 hours instead of an estimated 10, within the Batch API's 24-hour window.

iterations.title: 8. Consensus from independent agents
iterations.what: A different model family re-labels a blind 2,000-review sample. A third model adjudicates disagreements (capped at 200), and the majority of three decides. 200 adjudicated; the enricher was upheld by majority on topic in 130 and on intent in 172. The disagreements are analyzed, not hidden.

iterations.title: 9. Advisor pattern: test before trusting a stronger model
iterations.what: A stronger model was asked to finalize the cheap model's uncertain cases. On the 9 human-labeled flagged cases it made intent worse (6 correct to 4), so it was not adopted.

iterations.title: 10. A valid record can still be wrong
iterations.what: The memo's automatic checks caught a cut quote, rounded numbers, and a truncated draft. The author reviewed v3 and chose which improvements to make (A-D accepted, E rejected). An evidence-checker agent (Claude Haiku) now screens memo examples: 48 candidates checked, 8 rejected, including the paying user's bug report that had been quoted as a Premium restriction.

iterations.title: 11. Agents must be contained by code
iterations.what: The model sometimes broke the contract ('praise / unclear / pure request ⇒ severity 1'); a code rule fixed 3,350 cases and kept the model's value for audit. The course checker found 259 batch calls logged twice after an interrupted collection; the ledger is now read through a de-duplicating view, and the collector no longer re-logs.

iterations.title: 12. A capped fallback for the hard cases
iterations.what: The 1,583 nonempty reviews that failed the first pass (mostly long reviews and exact quotes) were re-run once with a declared stronger setting (effort low, 10 per request; a 10-case test first, then the rest). It rescued 1,499 for $0.1473; 84 remain visible as unresolved.

iterations.title: 13. LLMs are probabilistic: measure the run-to-run noise
iterations.what: analysis_10000.csv was re-classified from an empty cache with the same configuration. It gave the same topic for 93.2%, the same intent for 96.1%, and the same severity for 94.3% of 9,964 reviews. This is a ceiling for any agreement metric, and it also serves as the formal 500 and 10,000 checkpoint measurement.
